new_results.statement: For C=C3(A), ||C||op>=1. Splitting C by row/column triple overlap h gives some overlap operator norm >=1/4. The h=3 branch selects a principal triple |det|>=1/4; h=0 physicalizes to a disjoint cross block e3>=1/1024; h=1 selects one actual physical singleton star with fixed-s disjoint residual packet >=1/2304; h=2 selects one actual physical pair H with W_H^(2)>=1/144. The star selections are dimension-free because each triple belongs to exactly three singleton or pair stars.

On the h=2 operator branch, W_H^(2)>=1/144 for an actual physical pair. If m_H=max(|A_ii|,|A_jj|,|A_ij|)>=1/64, the completed r37 fixed-pair receiver gives ||p_Q||inf<482.184. The only h=2 survivor is m_H<1/64 with W_H^(2)>=1/144. Essential boundedness only; continuity not claimed.

On the h=1 operator branch one actual physical coordinate s supports a disjoint residual packet >=1/2304. If a=A_ss!=0, exactly a^2 e2(SS^T)>=1/2304 for the true scalar Schur cross S; if a=0, exactly ||u||^2||w||^2||P_u M P_w||F^2>=1/2304. If |a|>=1/64 and one Schur-E2 determinant-law side has inclusion marginals <=3/4, the r25 half-Riesz receiver plus scalar peel gives ||p_Q||inf<=125.483.

For the normalized three-flat-bank rank-three family, ||C^[h]||op=binom(3,h)(m-1)^(3-h)/m^3, so h=0 operator norm tends to one while h=2 tends to zero. Thus the r37 family that defeats W2-only pair selection is automatically routed to the disjoint paid branch by the operator-overlap funnel.
